lists.title: Catalan A1 Grammar Path
lists.description: A1 grammar in communicative order: pronouns (and when to drop them), noun gender and number, both article families, ser and tenir, the conjugation families, negation, hi ha, questions, and adjective agreement.

points.title: Subject pronouns (jo, tu, ell…)
points.function: Say who you are talking about — when it needs saying
points.explanation: Jo (I), tu (you, informal), ell/ella (he/she), vostè (you, formal), nosaltres (we), vosaltres (you all), vostès (you all, formal), ells/elles (they). The verb ending already names the person, so Catalan usually drops the pronoun — parlo català — and uses it only for emphasis or contrast.
points.culture_note: Vostè takes third-person verb forms, like Spanish usted — but Catalans reach for it less often than Spaniards do.

points.title: Gender and number of nouns
points.function: Name people and things, one or many
points.explanation:
Every noun is masculine or feminine, and the ending is only a clue; feminines often end in -a (casa), masculines in a consonant or -e (gat, llibre). El dia and el problema are masculine, and consonant endings go both ways (el sol, la sal), so learn each noun with its article.

| Singular ends in | Plural | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unstressed -a | -es | casa → cases |
| a stressed vowel | -ns | jardí → jardins |
| a stressed -s, -ç, -x, -tx | -os | gos → gossos |
| anything else | -s | llibre → llibres |

Spelling shifts keep the sound in the -es plurals: plaça → places, amiga → amigues. A few borrowings just add -s: cafè → cafès.

references.title: GIEC — Gramàtica de la llengua catalana (IEC)

drills.translation: I have two books.

points.title: Definite articles (el / la / els / les)
points.function: Point to a specific thing
points.explanation:
| Article | Before | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| el | masculine singular | el llibre |
| la | feminine singular | la casa |
| els | masculine plural | els llibres |
| les | feminine plural | les cases |

Before a vowel or an h both singulars shrink to **l'** (l'amic, l'escola, l'home) — except that la keeps its full form before an unstressed i- or u-: la idea, la universitat.

Catalan even puts an article before people's names in speech: la Maria, en Joan.
points.culture_note: The 'personal article' (en/na or el/la before names) is a very Catalan touch — la Núria arriba demà.

points.title: Indefinite articles (un / una)
points.function: Mention something for the first time
points.explanation:
| Article | Before | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| un | masculine singular | un gos |
| una | feminine singular | una casa |
| uns | masculine plural | uns amics |
| unes | feminine plural | unes cases |

Uns and unes mean 'some'. No elision here — una idea and una hora keep the article whole.

points.title: Ser — present (soc, ets, és…)
points.function: Say who or what someone is
points.explanation:
**Ser** (to be):

| Person | Form |
| --- | --- |
| jo | soc |
| tu | ets |
| ell / ella | és |
| nosaltres | som |
| vosaltres | sou |
| ells / elles | són |

Since the 2016 spelling reform, soc has no accent; és and són keep theirs to stay apart from es (the reflexive pronoun) and son ('sleepiness').

Professions take no article: ella és professora. Location can take ser too — són a casa 'they are at home'.

references.title: GIEC — Gramàtica de la llengua catalana (IEC)

points.title: Tenir — present (tinc gana)
points.function: Say what you have — and how you feel
points.explanation:
**Tenir** (to have):

| Person | Form |
| --- | --- |
| jo | tinc |
| tu | tens |
| ell / ella | té |
| nosaltres | tenim |
| vosaltres | teniu |
| ells / elles | tenen |

Catalan HAS its states: tenir gana (be hungry), tenir set (be thirsty), tenir raó (be right), tenir vint anys (be twenty).

points.title: Present tense of -ar verbs
points.function: Talk about what people do
points.explanation:
The biggest family.

Drop `-ar` and add:

| Person | Ending | parlar |
| --- | --- | --- |
| jo | -o | parlo |
| tu | -es | parles |
| ell / ella | -a | parla |
| nosaltres | -em | parlem |
| vosaltres | -eu | parleu |
| ells / elles | -en | parlen |

The ending names the person, so the pronoun usually stays home.

Verbs in -car, -gar, -çar and -jar respell the stem before an e: buscar → busques, jugar → jugues, començar → comences, menjar → menges.

points.title: -re and -ir verbs (perdre, dormir, llegir)
points.function: Sleep, read, hear — the other families
points.explanation:
| Person | perdre | dormir | llegir |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| jo | perdo | dormo | llegeixo |
| tu | perds | dorms | llegeixes |
| ell / ella | perd | dorm | llegeix |
| nosaltres | perdem | dormim | llegim |
| vosaltres | perdeu | dormiu | llegiu |
| ells / elles | perden | dormen | llegeixen |

The `-eix-` of llegir drops out in the nosaltres and vosaltres forms. Preferir follows llegir; sentir follows dormir.

Many verbs of this family take -c in the jo form: prendre → prenc, escriure → escric. Escriure keeps a v in escrivim and escriviu, but not in escriuen.

points.title: Negation with no
points.function: Say what is not so
points.explanation: No goes directly before the verb: no parlo anglès, no tinc temps. Emphatic denial can add pas after the verb (no vindrà pas), a very Catalan flourish you'll hear more than need.

points.title: Hi ha — there is / there are
points.function: Say what exists or is available
points.explanation:
Hi ha covers 'there is' and 'there are' — invariable: hi ha un llibre, hi ha dos cafès. Negative: no hi ha pa. Never hi han, however often you hear it.

The little hi is the same locative pronoun that makes Catalan Catalan.

points.title: Question words (on, com, què…)
points.function: Ask about places, people, time, and reasons
points.explanation: On (where), com (how), què (what), quan (when), per què (why), quant/quanta/quants/quantes (how much/many), qui (who). Question word first, verb next: On vius? Per què asks the question; perquè, written as one word, means 'because'.

points.title: Adjective agreement
points.function: Describe people and things correctly
points.explanation:
Four-form adjectives follow the noun pattern:

| Number | Masculine | Feminine |
| --- | --- | --- |
| singular | nou | nova |
| plural | nous | noves |

Others keep one singular form for both genders (amable, gran), but a consonant ending is no guarantee of that: calent, net and blau all take a feminine in -a (calenta, neta, blava).

Adjectives usually follow the noun: una casa blanca.

references.title: GIEC — Gramàtica de la llengua catalana (IEC)

drills.translation: The house is white.
The books are new.
My sister is very kind.
The coffee is hot.
The flowers are pretty.
The film is interesting.
The sky is blue.
The door is open.
The plates are clean.
The houses are small.

points.title: The present perfect (el perfet)
points.function: Talk about what has happened (today, recently)
points.explanation:
The perfet = the present of **haver** + the past participle: he menjat 'I have eaten'.

| Person | Form |
| --- | --- |
| jo | he |
| tu | has |
| ell / ella | ha |
| nosaltres | hem |
| vosaltres | heu |
| ells / elles | han |

Participles: -ar → -at, -re/-er → -ut, -ir → -it.

Common irregulars: fer → fet, dir → dit, veure → vist, escriure → escrit, obrir → obert.

Catalan uses the perfet for a recent or today's action, and the periphrastic past for earlier ones.

references.title: GIEC — Gramàtica de la llengua catalana (IEC)

This morning I drank a coffee.

Have you seen a film today?
He lost his keys.
She sang a beautiful song.
We visited the museum.

points.title: The past (passat perifràstic: vaig anar)
points.function: Talk about completed past actions
points.explanation:
Catalan's most characteristic tense: the past is built from an auxiliary plus the infinitive, not a participle — vaig menjar 'I ate', va anar 'he went'.

| Person | Auxiliary |
| --- | --- |
| jo | vaig |
| tu | vas |
| ell / ella | va |
| nosaltres | vam |
| vosaltres | vau |
| ells / elles | van |

The auxiliary is the present of anar, except that nosaltres and vosaltres take vam and vau, not anem and aneu. Vam, vau and van also appear as vàrem, vàreu and varen.

It's the normal past for earlier actions, unlike Spanish or French.

points.title: The imperfect (l'imperfet)
points.function: Describe ongoing or habitual past actions
points.explanation:
The **imperfet** describes a past that was ongoing, repeated, or a background — English 'was …-ing' / 'used to'. Contrast it with the periphrastic past, which reports one completed act.

Verbs in -ar take the first set of endings; verbs in -re, -er and -ir take the second.

| person | menjar | dormir |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I | menjava | dormia |
| you (sg.) | menjaves | dormies |
| he / she | menjava | dormia |
| we | menjàvem | dormíem |
| you (pl.) | menjàveu | dormíeu |
| they | menjaven | dormien |

A handful of verbs build it on an irregular stem: ser → era, fer → feia, dir → deia, veure → veia, dur → duia.

references.title: GIEC — Gramàtica de la llengua catalana (IEC)

points.title: The future (el futur)
points.function: Talk about what will happen
points.explanation:
The **futur** adds one set of endings to the infinitive: menjaré 'I will eat', dormirà 'he will sleep'. A verb in -re drops that final -e first: perdre gives perdré, veure gives veurem.

| person | ending | menjar |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I | -é | menjaré |
| you (sg.) | -às | menjaràs |
| he / she | -à | menjarà |
| we | -em | menjarem |
| you (pl.) | -eu | menjareu |
| they | -an | menjaran |

Some verbs replace the infinitive with an irregular stem: anar → aniré, tenir → tindré, venir → vindré, fer → faré, poder → podré, voler → voldré.

references.title: GIEC — Gramàtica de la llengua catalana (IEC)

drills.translation: Tomorrow I will go to work early.
Tonight we will watch a film together.
Will you come with us on the trip?
Anna will buy the gift tomorrow.

points.title: Weak pronouns — direct object (el, la, els, les)
points.function: Replace the object with a weak pronoun
points.explanation:
A known direct object becomes a weak pronoun standing before the verb: El veig 'I see him'.

| object | pronoun |
| --- | --- |
| me | em |
| you (sg.) | et |
| him, it (m.) | el |
| her, it (f.) | la |
| us | ens |
| you (pl.) | us |
| them (m.) | els |
| them (f.) | les |

Before a vowel or h, em, et and el elide: m'ajuda, t'espero, l'he vist. la elides too, except before an unstressed i- or u- (la imitem); ens, us, els and les never elide.

After the verb the pronoun attaches to it, with a hyphen (rentar-lo, renta-la) or, after a vowel where a shortened form exists, with an apostrophe (mira'l 'look at him', renta'ls).

references.title: GIEC — Gramàtica de la llengua catalana (IEC)

points.title: Weak pronouns — en and hi
points.function: Replace a quantity/'of it' and a place
points.explanation:
en replaces de + something, or a quantity: en vull 'I want some', en tinc tres 'I have three of them'. Before a vowel it elides to n': n'he comprat un quilo 'I've bought a kilo of them'.

hi replaces a place, or a complement introduced by a, en or amb: hi vaig 'I go there', no hi penso 'I don't think about it' (from pensar en), no hi estic d'acord 'I don't agree with it'. hi never elides.

Both are very common and often untranslated in English.

points.title: Comparative & superlative (més… que, el més)
points.function: Compare things
points.explanation:
The comparative uses més 'more' or menys 'less' + adjective + que 'than': més gran que 'bigger than'.

The superlative adds the definite article, which agrees with the noun: el més gran, la més gran 'the biggest'. When the adjective follows its noun the article is not repeated, and the group compared against takes de: el cafè més bo de la ciutat 'the best café in town'.

Irregulars: bo → millor 'better', dolent → pitjor 'worse'.

points.title: Reflexive verbs (rentar-se)
points.function: Say the subject acts on itself
points.explanation:
A reflexive verb carries a weak pronoun matching its subject, placed before the verb.

| person | pronoun |
| --- | --- |
| I | em |
| you (sg.) | et |
| he / she | es |
| we | ens |
| you (pl.) | us |
| they | es |

Em rento 'I wash (myself)', es lleva 'he gets up', ens quedem 'we stay'. Before a vowel em, et and es elide (m'aixeco, t'aixeques, s'aixeca); ens and us do not. The infinitive carries the pronoun after it, joined by a hyphen: rentar-se, llevar-se.

Many daily-routine verbs are reflexive.

points.title: Contractions (al, del, pel)
points.function: Combine a preposition with the article
points.explanation:
The prepositions a, de, per contract with the masculine articles el/els: a + el = al, a + els = als, de + el = del, de + els = dels, per + el = pel, per + els = pels.

Vaig al cinema 'I go to the cinema'; la casa dels avis 'the grandparents' house'. They never contract with la/les or l'.

drills.translation: I'm going to the cinema tonight.

The book is the teacher's.
We walk through the park every afternoon.
I come back from work at six.
We give food to the birds.

points.title: Possessives & demonstratives (el meu, aquest…)
points.function: Say 'my / this' and agree with the noun
points.explanation:
Possessives take the definite article and agree with the thing owned, not the owner: el meu llibre, les meves germanes.

| owner | m. sg. | f. sg. | m. pl. | f. pl. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| my | meu | meva | meus | meves |
| your (sg.) | teu | teva | teus | teves |
| his, her, its, their | seu | seva | seus | seves |
| our | nostre | nostra | nostres | nostres |
| your (pl.) | vostre | vostra | vostres | vostres |

points.title: The subjunctive (el subjuntiu)
points.function: Express opinion, wish, doubt, and emotion
points.explanation:
After verbs of wish, doubt, emotion or need — vull que, dubto que, m'alegro que, cal que — Catalan uses the subjunctive. So do the conjunctions encara que 'although', abans que 'before' and perquè 'so that'.

| person | parlar | perdre | dormir |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| I | parli | perdi | dormi |
| you (sg.) | parlis | perdis | dormis |
| he / she | parli | perdi | dormi |
| we | parlem | perdem | dormim |
| you (pl.) | parleu | perdeu | dormiu |
| they | parlin | perdin | dormin |

Key irregulars: ser (sigui), haver (hagi), fer (faci), anar (vagi), poder (pugui), tenir (tingui), venir (vingui), dir (digui), voler (vulgui), saber (sàpiga).

points.title: The conditional (el condicional)
points.function: Say what you would do; be polite
points.explanation:
The **condicional** puts the imperfect endings -ia, -ies, -ia, -íem, -íeu, -ien on the stem the future uses: the infinitive for regular verbs, the irregular stem for the rest.

| person | menjar | venir |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I | menjaria | vindria |
| you (sg.) | menjaries | vindries |
| he / she | menjaria | vindria |
| we | menjaríem | vindríem |
| you (pl.) | menjaríeu | vindríeu |
| they | menjarien | vindrien |

It softens requests (voldria 'I would like', podries 'could you') and states hypotheticals.

points.title: Combined weak pronouns (me'l, l'hi, se'n)
points.function: Combine two weak pronouns before the verb
points.explanation:
Catalan is famous for stacking weak pronouns. The indirect one comes first, and before another pronoun em, et and es take the forms me, te and se.

| pronouns | combined |
| --- | --- |
| em + el | me'l |
| et + el | te'l |
| li + el | l'hi |
| li + la | l'hi |
| em + en | me'n |
| es + en | se'n |

Me'l dones 'you give it to me', te'l porto 'I bring it to you', l'hi dono 'I give it to him', se'n va 'he goes away'.

points.title: The imperative (parla! no parlis!)
points.function: Give commands and instructions
points.explanation:
The command has a form of its own for each addressee, and the negative always uses the subjunctive.

| addressee | affirmative | negative |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tu | parla | no parlis |
| vostè | parli | no parli |
| vosaltres | parleu | no parleu |
| vostès | parlin | no parlin |

The tu form is the third-person singular of the present indicative (parla! 'speak!', obre! 'open!'); vosaltres uses the second-person plural (parleu!, obriu!); vostè and vostès use the subjunctive (parli!, obri!).

A few tu forms are irregular: ser → sigues, tenir → tingues, fer → fes, dir → digues, venir → vine, anar → ves.

points.title: The past perfect (el plusquamperfet)
points.function: Set one past action before another
points.explanation:
The **plusquamperfet** ('had done') is the imperfet of haver plus the past participle. It marks an action completed before another past moment: quan vas arribar, jo ja havia sopat.

| person | form |
| --- | --- |
| I | havia menjat |
| you (sg.) | havies menjat |
| he / she | havia menjat |
| we | havíem menjat |
| you (pl.) | havíeu menjat |
| they | havien menjat |

Catalan builds every compound tense with haver — there is no ser auxiliary as in French or Italian, and the participle does not change with the subject.

points.title: The gerund (el gerundi: fent)
points.function: Say 'while / by doing' and mark ongoing action
points.explanation:
The gerund ending follows the verb's conjugation:

- Verbs in `-ar` take `-ant`: menjant 'eating'
- Verbs in `-er` and `-re` take `-ent`: perdent 'losing'
- Verbs in `-ir` take `-int`: llegint 'reading'

Alone it means 'while / by …-ing': s'aprèn viatjant 'you learn by travelling'.

With estar it makes the progressive: estic menjant 'I'm eating'. (Avoid the gerund of consequence — it's an error.)

points.title: Subjunctive after conjunctions

The subjunctive has past forms. After a PAST main verb those same triggers move to the imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive: volia que vingués, no pensava que hagués vingut. This is the concordança dels temps.

The daily irregulars, in the order jo, tu, ell/ella, nosaltres, vosaltres, ells/elles:

- anar (to go): vaig, vas, va, anem, aneu, van
- fer (to do/make): faig, fas, fa, fem, feu, fan
- poder (can): puc, pots, pot, podem, podeu, poden
- voler (to want): vull, vols, vol, volem, voleu, volen

- dir (to say): dic, dius, diu, diem, dieu, diuen

points.title: Estar — states and location (estic cansat)
points.function: Say how and where things are right now
points.explanation:
**Estar**:

| Person | Form |
| --- | --- |
| jo | estic |
| tu | estàs |
| ell / ella | està |
| nosaltres | estem |
| vosaltres | esteu |
| ells / elles | estan |

Use it for temporary states and conditions (Estic cansat, La Maria està malalta) and for where someone is right now (Els nens estan a l'escola). Identity, origin, and permanent qualities stay with ser: Soc de Barcelona. És alta.

estar + gerundi says what's happening right now: Estic llegint.
points.culture_note: Catalan draws the ser/estar line differently from Spanish — location of things often takes ser (El llibre és a la taula), while people right now take estar.

related.title: Ser — present (soc, ets, és…)
related.contrast: ser for identity and origin; estar for states and being somewhere now.
